critical_code_review_comments: publish endpoint: asyncio.create_task(_run_broadcast()) is fire-and-forget with no reference retained — if the event loop is short-lived (it isn't here, but on some ASGI servers) the task could be GC'd mid-flight. Consider storing the task on an app-level set to keep a strong reference (Python asyncio.create_task returns a Task the caller is expected to keep). Low risk in FastAPI + uvicorn but worth noting.

publish endpoint: broadcast_queued is pre-counted with db.users.count_documents(...) which double-scans users (once for the count, again inside the async iterator). Fine for now; if the user base grows past ~100k consider dropping the pre-count and returning `broadcastQueued: -1` or just an estimate.

rca of the issue: Bug #1 root cause: content.js._semexRenderOutdatedUI previously fell through to _semexShowUpdateBanner on non-gateway hosts, so opening the Railway admin panel (a non-gateway host) rendered an in-page 'extension too old' banner. Fix: single-branch — call _semexShowUpdatePaywall only when _semexIsGatewayHost(). Bug #2 root cause: publish() awaited an async-for loop over db.users, calling send_message per user serially inside the request handler. On a real user base this exceeded Railway's ingress timeout so the browser spinner never resolved. Fix: pre-count queued users, then asyncio.create_task(_run_broadcast()) so publish returns immediately with `broadcastQueued: count`. Measured elapsed on empty user table: ~0.03s (was previously O(users) with per-user Telegram send latency ~200-500ms each).
